metadata.description: TP-G2 demo subset: 72 frozen factorial programs (3 per discipline x container cell) and 28 placed survivor-family programs, with their teacher-forced program states (Qwen3-8B bf16 block 17 / Qwen3-32B NF4 block 33 and the layer, readout, E0, RANDNET and second-context arrays the analysis uses).

state_storage.format: states[key] = coordinates of the program's state in an exact isometric basis (thin uncentred SVD of the selected programs' own states for that key); key = '<model>|<readout>|<block>', '<model>|E0', 'randnet|R1|17' or '8b_ctx2|R1|17'
state_storage.preserves: inner products, norms, cosine and Euclidean distances (rounded to 9 significant digits)

readouts.R1g: R1 without massive-activation tokens (norm > 10x the sequence median)
readouts.R2: token after the first pop/popleft/heappop/get call

BFSO-DEQUE.S: Keep the frontier in a collections.deque.
BFSO-DEQUE.R: Add every newly discovered cell at the right end with append() and always take the next cell to expand from the left end with popleft(), so cells are expanded strictly in first-in first-out order.
BFSO-DEQUE.V: Mark a cell as seen at the moment it is added to the deque and record its parent then.
BFSO-DEQUE.E: Do not use heapq, a set as the frontier, or recursion.

BFSO-LIST.S: Keep the frontier in a plain Python list; do not import collections or heapq.
BFSO-LIST.R: Append every newly discovered cell to the end of the list and take the next cell from the front, either with list.pop(0) or by advancing an integer head index into the list, so cells are expanded in first-in first-out order.
BFSO-LIST.V: Mark a cell as seen at the moment it is appended and record its parent then.
BFSO-LIST.E: Do not use a deque, heapq or recursion.

BFSO-HEAP.S: Keep the frontier in a heapq heap of tuples (counter, row, col), where counter is an integer that increases by one every time any cell is pushed.
BFSO-HEAP.R: Always pop the entry with the smallest counter, so cells come out in exactly the order in which they were inserted (first-in first-out); the counter is the only key, with no distances and no estimates.
BFSO-HEAP.V: Mark a cell as seen when it is pushed, never push a seen cell again, and record its parent then.
BFSO-HEAP.E: Do not use a deque or recursion, and do not compare or update distances.

BFSO-GRID2D.S: Store the search state only in 2-D lists the size of the grid: a level array initialised to -1 and a parent array; do not use any queue, deque, heap, set or list of frontier cells.
BFSO-GRID2D.R: Set the level of the start cell to 0. Then for d = 0, 1, 2, ... scan every cell of the grid row by row, and for every cell whose level equals d give each free neighbour whose level is still -1 the level d + 1 and record its parent. Stop when the goal has a level or when a whole scan assigns nothing.
BFSO-GRID2D.V: A cell counts as visited once its level is no longer -1.
BFSO-GRID2D.E: Rebuild the returned path by following parent links back from the goal to the start.

BFSO-SET.S: Keep the current frontier as a Python set and build the next frontier as a new set; keep a set of visited cells and a parent dict.
BFSO-SET.R: Work level by level: expand every cell of the current frontier set, put each free unvisited neighbour into the next-frontier set, then replace the frontier by the next-frontier set. Stop as soon as the goal is reached or the frontier is empty.
BFSO-SET.V: Mark a cell visited when it is added to the next frontier and record its parent then.
BFSO-SET.E: Do not use a deque, heapq, a list used as a queue, or recursion.

DFSO-DEQUE.S: Keep the frontier in a collections.deque that is used as a stack.
DFSO-DEQUE.R: Push every newly discovered cell at the right end with append() and always take the next cell from the same right end with pop(), so the most recently discovered cell is expanded first (last-in first-out) and the search goes as deep as possible before it backs up.
DFSO-DEQUE.V: Mark a cell visited when it is pushed and record its parent then; never push a visited cell.
DFSO-DEQUE.E: Do not use popleft(), heapq or recursion.

DFSO-LIST.S: Keep the frontier in a plain Python list used as a stack; do not import collections or heapq.
DFSO-LIST.R: Append every newly discovered cell to the end of the list and always take the next cell from the end with list.pop(), so the most recently discovered cell is expanded first (last-in first-out) and the search goes as deep as possible before it backs up.
DFSO-LIST.V: Mark a cell visited when it is pushed and record its parent then; never push a visited cell.
DFSO-LIST.E: Do not use pop(0), a deque or recursion.

DFSO-CALL.S: Use a recursive helper function and the call stack only; do not use any explicit stack, queue, deque, heap or list of frontier cells.
DFSO-CALL.R: The helper is called on a cell, marks it visited and, for each free unvisited neighbour in turn, calls itself recursively on that neighbour before trying the next neighbour; it returns as soon as the goal is reached.
DFSO-CALL.V: Keep visited cells in a set or a 2-D boolean array and build the path from the recursion (keep a path list that is extended before each call and shortened after it, or prepend cells on the way back).
DFSO-CALL.E: Grids can be 30x30, so raise the recursion limit with sys.setrecursionlimit.

DFSO-HEAP.S: Keep the frontier in a heapq heap of tuples (key, row, col), where key = -counter and counter is an integer that increases by one at every push.
DFSO-HEAP.R: Always pop the entry with the smallest key, that is the most recently pushed cell, so the heap behaves as a last-in first-out stack and the search goes as deep as possible first.
DFSO-HEAP.V: Mark a cell visited when it is pushed and record its parent then; never push a visited cell.
DFSO-HEAP.E: Use no distances, no estimates, no relaxation and no recursion.

HEUR-HEAP.S: Keep the frontier in a heapq heap of tuples (key, counter, row, col), where counter is only a tie-breaker that increases at every push.
HEUR-HEAP.R: Always pop the frontier cell with the smallest key, where {KEY}
HEUR-HEAP.E: Do not use a deque or recursion.

HEUR-LIST.S: Keep the frontier in a plain Python list; do not import heapq or collections.
HEUR-LIST.R: At every step select the frontier cell with the smallest key, either by keeping the list sorted with bisect.insort on (key, counter, row, col) tuples and taking its first element, or by scanning the whole list for the minimum key and removing it with pop(i); here {KEY}
HEUR-LIST.E: Do not use heapq, a deque or recursion.

HEUR-GRID2D.S: Store the search state only in 2-D lists the size of the grid: an open-flag array, a closed-flag array, a steps array and a parent array; do not use any queue, deque, heap, set or list of frontier cells.
HEUR-GRID2D.R: At every step scan the whole grid row by row for the open cell with the smallest key, close it, and open each free neighbour that is not closed (updating its steps and parent when it is new or its steps improve); here {KEY}
HEUR-GRID2D.V: Stop when the goal is closed or no open cell remains.
HEUR-GRID2D.E: Rebuild the returned path by following parent links back from the goal to the start.

HEUR-SET.S: Keep the open (frontier) cells in a Python set, with dicts for parents and step counts.
HEUR-SET.R: At every step take the open cell with the smallest key using min(open_cells, key=...), remove it from the set and add its free neighbours that were not expanded yet (updating steps and parent when they are new or improve); here {KEY}
HEUR-SET.V: Keep a set of expanded cells and never expand a cell twice.
HEUR-SET.E: Do not use heapq, a deque or recursion.

COST-HEAP.S: Keep a dict (or 2-D list) dist with the best known number of steps from the start, and a heapq heap of (dist, row, col) tuples.
COST-HEAP.R: Repeatedly pop the entry with the smallest distance; if its distance is larger than the recorded dist of that cell it is a stale entry and is skipped. For each free neighbour compute new = d + 1, and if new < dist[neighbour] (unknown cells count as infinity) set dist[neighbour] = new, record the parent and push (new, neighbour). The key is the step count from the start only: there is no estimate toward the goal.
COST-HEAP.V: Stop when the goal is popped.
COST-HEAP.E: Rebuild the returned path by following parent links back from the goal to the start.

COST-LIST.S: Keep dist (best known steps from the start) in a dict or 2-D list and the frontier in a plain Python list of cells; do not import heapq or collections.
COST-LIST.R: At every step scan the frontier list for the cell with the smallest dist, remove it with pop(i) and skip it if it was already finalised; for each free neighbour, if dist[cell] + 1 < dist[neighbour] (unknown cells count as infinity), update dist and parent and append the neighbour to the list. No estimate toward the goal is used.
COST-LIST.V: Stop when the goal is finalised.
COST-LIST.E: Rebuild the returned path by following parent links back from the goal to the start.

COST-GRID2D.S: Store dist (initialised to infinity, start = 0), a done flag and the parent in 2-D lists the size of the grid; do not use any queue, deque, heap, set or list of frontier cells.
COST-GRID2D.R: At every step scan the whole grid row by row for the not-done cell with the smallest finite dist, mark it done, and for each free neighbour, if dist[cell] + 1 < dist[neighbour], update dist and parent. No estimate toward the goal is used.
COST-GRID2D.V: Stop when the goal is done or no not-done cell with a finite dist remains.
COST-GRID2D.E: Rebuild the returned path by following parent links back from the goal to the start.

COST-SET.S: Keep the open cells in a Python set and the best known distances from the start in a dict.
COST-SET.R: At every step take u = min(open_cells, key=lambda c: dist[c]), remove it from the set, and for each free neighbour v, if dist[u] + 1 < dist.get(v, infinity), set dist[v] and parent[v] and add v to the open set. No estimate toward the goal is used.
COST-SET.V: Stop when the goal is removed from the open set.
COST-SET.E: Do not use heapq, a deque or recursion.

RELAX-GRID2D.S: Store dist (initialised to infinity, start = 0) and the parent only in 2-D lists the size of the grid; do not use any queue, deque, heap, set or list of frontier cells, and no recursion.
RELAX-GRID2D.R: Repeat full passes over the grid: in each pass visit every cell row by row and, for every free cell with a finite dist, try each free neighbour: if dist[cell] + 1 < dist[neighbour], set dist[neighbour] = dist[cell] + 1 and record the parent. Stop when a complete pass changes nothing (or after rows*cols passes).
RELAX-GRID2D.V: Every pass processes all cells; there is no frontier.
RELAX-GRID2D.E: Rebuild the returned path by following parent links back from the goal to the start.

RELAX-LIST.S: Build once, at the start, an explicit Python list of directed edges (u, v) between adjacent free cells, and keep dist (start = 0, others infinity) and parent in a dict or 2-D list.
RELAX-LIST.R: Then repeat rounds: in each round loop over the entire edge list and, whenever dist[u] + 1 < dist[v], set dist[v] = dist[u] + 1 and parent[v] = u. Stop when a whole round changes nothing (or after number-of-cells - 1 rounds).
RELAX-LIST.V: Every round processes all edges; there is no frontier, queue or heap.
RELAX-LIST.E: Rebuild the returned path by following parent links back from the goal to the start.

RELAX-SET.S: Keep the set of all free cells in a Python set and the distances in a dict (start = 0, a missing cell counts as infinity).
RELAX-SET.R: Repeat full sweeps: in each sweep iterate over every cell of the set of free cells and, for every neighbour of a cell with a known distance, if dist[cell] + 1 < dist.get(neighbour, infinity), update dist and parent. Stop when a whole sweep changes nothing.
RELAX-SET.V: Every sweep visits all free cells; there is no frontier, queue or heap.
RELAX-SET.E: Rebuild the returned path by following parent links back from the goal to the start.

RAND-LIST.S: Keep the frontier in a plain Python list; do not import heapq or collections.
RAND-LIST.R: At every step remove a uniformly random element of the list (i = random.randrange(len(frontier)), then pop(i), or swap it with the last element and pop) and expand it; there is no ordering rule other than chance.
RAND-LIST.V: Mark a cell as seen when it is added and record its parent then.
RAND-LIST.E: Use the random module and never call random.seed.

RAND-HEAP.S: Keep the frontier in a heapq heap of tuples (random_key, row, col), where random_key = random.random() is drawn fresh when the cell is pushed.
RAND-HEAP.R: Always pop the smallest random key, so the expansion order is random.
RAND-HEAP.V: Mark a cell as seen when it is pushed and record its parent then.
RAND-HEAP.E: Never call random.seed; use no distances and no estimates.

RAND-SET.S: Keep the frontier in a Python set.
RAND-SET.R: At every step pick c = random.choice(tuple(frontier)), a uniformly random member, remove it from the set and expand it.
RAND-SET.V: Mark a cell as seen when it is added and record its parent then.
RAND-SET.E: Never call random.seed; do not use heapq or a deque.

RAND-DEQUE.S: Keep the frontier in a collections.deque.
RAND-DEQUE.R: At every step rotate the deque by a random amount, frontier.rotate(random.randrange(len(frontier))), and then take the cell at the left end with popleft().
RAND-DEQUE.V: Mark a cell as seen when it is added and record its parent then.
RAND-DEQUE.E: Never call random.seed; do not use heapq.

A move goes to one of the 4 orthogonal neighbours (up, down, left, right) and may not leave the grid or enter a wall. Return a list of (row, col) tuples that begins with start, ends with goal, and in which consecutive cells are neighbours and every cell is free. Any valid path is accepted; it does not have to be the shortest. If start equals goal and the cell is free, return [start]. If no path exists, or start or goal is a wall, return [].

from collections import deque

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0]) if rows > 0 else 0
    if not (0 <= start[0] < rows and 0 <= start[1] < cols) or not (0 <= goal[0] < rows and 0 <= goal[1] < cols) or grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or (grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#'):
        return []
    if start == goal:
        return [start]
    frontier = deque()
    parent = {}
    seen = set()
    directions = [(0, 1), (1, 0), (0, -1), (-1, 0)]
    frontier.append(start)
    seen.add(start)
    while frontier:
        current = frontier.popleft()
        if current == goal:
            path = []
            while current in parent:
                path.append(current)
                current = parent[current]
            path.append(start)
            return path[::-1]
        r, c = current
        for dr, dc in directions:
            nr, nc = (r + dr, c + dc)
            if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols and (grid[nr][nc] == '.') and ((nr, nc) not in seen):
                frontier.append((nr, nc))
                seen.add((nr, nc))
                parent[nr, nc] = current
    return []

import heapq

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    if start == goal:
        if 0 <= start[0] < len(grid) and 0 <= start[1] < len(grid[0]) and (grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '.'):
            return [start]
        return []
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    if not (0 <= start[0] < rows and 0 <= start[1] < cols and (grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '.')):
        return []
    if not (0 <= goal[0] < rows and 0 <= goal[1] < cols and (grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '.')):
        return []
    seen = set()
    parent = {}
    counter = 0
    frontier = []
    heapq.heappush(frontier, (counter, start[0], start[1]))
    seen.add(start)
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    while frontier:
        cnt, r, c = heapq.heappop(frontier)
        current = (r, c)
        if current == goal:
            path = []
            while current != start:
                path.append(current)
                current = parent[current]
            path.append(start)
            return path[::-1]
        for dr, dc in directions:
            nr, nc = (r + dr, c + dc)
            if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols and (grid[nr][nc] == '.') and ((nr, nc) not in seen):
                seen.add((nr, nc))
                parent[nr, nc] = current
                counter += 1
                heapq.heappush(frontier, (counter, nr, nc))
    return []

import random

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []
    if start == goal:
        return [start]
    rows, cols = (len(grid), len(grid[0]))
    seen = [[False for _ in range(cols)] for _ in range(rows)]
    parent = [[None for _ in range(cols)] for _ in range(rows)]
    frontier = [start]
    seen[start[0]][start[1]] = True
    while frontier:

        r, c = cell

            if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols and (not seen[nr][nc]) and (grid[nr][nc] == '.'):

                parent[nr][nc] = cell
                frontier.append((nr, nc))
                if (nr, nc) == goal:

                    current = goal
                    while current:

import collections
import random

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0]) if rows > 0 else 0
    if start == goal and grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '.':
        return [start]
    if not (0 <= start[0] < rows and 0 <= start[1] < cols) or not (0 <= goal[0] < rows and 0 <= goal[1] < cols) or grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or (grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#'):
        return []
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    frontier = collections.deque()
    frontier.append(start)
    came_from = {}
    came_from[start] = None
    while frontier:
        frontier.rotate(random.randrange(len(frontier)))
        current = frontier.popleft()
        if current == goal:
            break
        for dx, dy in directions:
            next_x = current[0] + dx
            next_y = current[1] + dy
            next_cell = (next_x, next_y)
            if 0 <= next_x < rows and 0 <= next_y < cols and (grid[next_x][next_y] == '.') and (next_cell not in came_from):
                came_from[next_cell] = current
                frontier.append(next_cell)
    if current != goal:
        return []
    path = []
    while current is not None:
        path.append(current)
        current = came_from[current]
    path.reverse()
    return path

import heapq
import random

def solve(grid, start, goal):
    if start[0] < 0 or start[0] >= len(grid) or start[1] < 0 or (start[1] >= len(grid[0])) or (grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#'):
        return []
    if start == goal:
        return [start]
    if goal[0] < 0 or goal[0] >= len(grid) or goal[1] < 0 or (goal[1] >= len(grid[0])) or (grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#'):
        return []
    directions = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    pq = []
    visited = set()
    heapq.heappush(pq, (random.random(), 0, start, [start]))
    visited.add(start)
    counter = 1
    while pq:
        priority, cnt, current, path = heapq.heappop(pq)
        current_row, current_col = current
        if current == goal:
            return path
        for dr, dc in directions:
            next_row, next_col = (current_row + dr, current_col + dc)
            next_cell = (next_row, next_col)
            if 0 <= next_row < len(grid) and 0 <= next_col < len(grid[0]) and (grid[next_row][next_col] == '.') and (next_cell not in visited):
                new_path = path + [next_cell]
                heapq.heappush(pq, (random.random(), counter, next_cell, new_path))
                visited.add(next_cell)
                counter += 1
    return []
